label: Scryfall-derived assessment - provisional
attribution: Card facts retrieved from Scryfall; color tiers are a Vox Mana/Codex judgment, not Scryfall or Wizards rankings.
owner_direction: Reasonable Scryfall-based judgments are authorized for Absorb; retain evidence/rationale, preserve 2021, no app changes.
supersedes: Prior A research packet Absorb row only, for the proposed research assessment. Earlier explicit-source-only result remains historically valid. No catalog or 2021 identity mapping is changed.

recommended_placements.name: White
recommended_placements.rationale: Primary is my provisional best-fit judgment: the only observed native source is a monowhite common that deliberately grants Absorb. White is therefore the best-supported home in this evidence set. Designer history also places the precursor armor designs in white. This supports a proposed home, not proof of a broad established tier.

recommended_placements.name: Blue
recommended_placements.rationale: No native blue Absorb source was found in the exact-word Scryfall population. Absorbing Man is a substring false positive, not the Absorb keyword. No secondary or tertiary assignment is justified.

recommended_placements.name: Black
recommended_placements.rationale: No native black Absorb source was found. A black Sliver receiving Absorb from Lymph Sliver is granted access from a white source, not evidence of native black ownership.

recommended_placements.name: Red
recommended_placements.rationale: No native red Absorb source was found. Receiving the granted ability, copying a card, or lacking observed cards does not establish a red tier.

recommended_placements.name: Green
recommended_placements.rationale: No native green Absorb source was found. General toughness, resilience, or damage-prevention similarities are not enough to assign this exact keyword a tier.

observed_population.basis: Card colors of the deliberate grant source, not colors of creatures that can receive the ability; deduplicate by oracle_id.

cards.name: Lymph Sliver
cards.evidence_summary: A white Sliver that grants absorb 1 to all Sliver creatures.

search_evidence.initial_keyword_queries: kw:absorb returned HTTP404 not_found (zero matches), including include:extras. Lymph Sliver has an empty keywords field despite granting absorb in Oracle text; keyword-only discovery misses it.
search_evidence.broad_query: o:absorb returned two unique cards. Exclude Absorbing Man: its text names itself but does not contain the keyword.
search_evidence.printings: o:absorb unique:prints returned four rows, two for each name. Only the two Lymph Sliver rows are relevant. They are one design, not two independent designs.
search_evidence.extras: Exact-word Oracle query with include:extras returned one card with has_more false.

supporting_design_context.title: Future Sight Design Handoff Document
supporting_design_context.author: Mark Rosewater
supporting_design_context.location: White / cW12 Full-Plate Paladin and uW13 Astral Elemental
supporting_design_context.summary: Rosewater identifies armor as the predecessor name for Absorb. The white handoff section contains armor concepts, including an unprinted armor-bearing version of Astral Elemental. These corroborate white design intent, but are not additional printed Scryfall cards or explicit P/S/T assignments.
supporting_design_context.use: Supporting qualitative context only; no 2021 Mechanical Color Pie tiers inherited.

limitations: One unique card is a very small sample. Two printings do not supply two independent color decisions.
Observed exclusivity supports white as a proposed home but does not prove whether R&D would classify it primary, secondary or tertiary.
Unassigned means not established by this evidence, not unavailable, colorless, zero access or a prohibition.
The classification concerns the exact keyword Absorb, not the counterspell named Absorb, general damage prevention, copying, or all potential recipients of a granted ability.
Absorb being scarce across all Magic does not automatically make it tertiary in its only demonstrated color.
Reassess after a new native design in another color, explicit designer tier guidance, or evidence of a deliberate color-pie exception.
